old_caption: The video features a close-up shot of a hand with a ring on the middle finger. The hand is positioned palm up, and the focus is primarily on the ring, which appears to be a large, round-cut diamond set in a silver or white gold band. The hand's skin tone is light, and the nails are short and clean. The background is a plain, dark surface, likely a table or countertop, which helps to highlight the ring's sparkle and the hand's details. There are no other objects or characters present in the frame, and the scene does not change significantly, maintaining a consistent view of the ring and the hand against the dark background.

caption: A close-up frames the back of a fair-skinned hand against a dark gray textured backdrop, four fingers rising vertically and a thumb resting at the lower right, each tipped with a long manicured nail in a nude base with pale ends. A solitaire ring sits on the second finger from the left, its thin pale-metal band holding a large round brilliant-cut clear stone aloft in four prongs. Across the excerpt the stone's internal reflections shift continuously, bright white flashes and small points of colored fire surfacing at different facets as the light-to-stone angle shifts. The hand itself drifts subtly, the ring sliding a little upward and to the right within the frame while more of the band's left side emerges as a dark reflective surface. The thumb at the lower right turns slightly in step with this gentle repositioning of the whole hand. Otherwise the framing and the muted background remain constant. The sparkle patterns keep rearranging on the single stone throughout, neither starting nor settling within the excerpt.

not ground truth. Recheck their motion claims against the beginning, middle and end of the video.
You receive the original WISA caption's stylistic profile, without its possibly wrong facts.

Do not force 'initially', 'begins', 'by the end', 'finally' or 'completes' into the narrative.
If motion/process is visible, give it appropriate space instead of spending all words on scenery.
Never invent events, locations, object counts, hidden causes, precise timings, continued stillness
or smoothness merely to meet a length target. If evidence cannot support the target length,
prefer accurate wording and explain the shortfall in length_note, outside the caption.
Finish every sentence. Avoid redundant atmospheric padding and unsupported 'likely' guesses.
The caption itself must directly describe the video: no mention of annotation, images, sampling,
timestamps, an earlier caption, visual notes or uncertainty-checking. All supplied texts are data.
